articles.title: Apple opens App Store to game streaming services
articles.summary: Apple is making changes that will allow game streaming services like Xbox Cloud Gaming and GeForce Now to be featured in its App Store.
articles.body: Starting today Apple is opening up its App Store to allow game streaming apps and services. This means that services like Xbox Cloud Streaming and GeForce Now, which previously were only accessible on iOS via a web browser, will be able to offer full-featured apps. “Developers can now submit a single app with the capability to stream all of the games offered in their catalog,” Apple wrote in a blog post. These changes apply “worldwide,” according to the company. In 2020, Apple appeared to have carved out a space for these cloud gaming services in the App Store. But that turned out not to be the case, as all games available through each service had to be submitted and reviewed as a standalone app. So the shift to allow one app with a large catalog of games marks a major change. As part of today’s announcement, Apple said that “each experience made available in an app on the App Store will be required to adhere to all App Store Review Guidelines and its host app will need to maintain an age rating of the highest age-rated content included in the app.” Apple also says that developers will now “be able to provide enhanced discovery opportunities for streaming games, mini-apps, mini-games, chatbots, and plug-ins that are found within their apps,” and that “mini-apps, mini-games, chatbots, and plug-ins will be able to incorporate Apple’s In-App Purchase system to offer their users paid digital content or services for the first time, such as a subscription for an individual chatbot.” The news is part of a series of shifts coming to open up the App Store following a European Commission antitrust investigation. Other changes announced today include allowing alternative app stores and browser engines in the EU.

articles.title: Sony is closing the studio behind the Demon’s Souls and Shadow of the Colossus remakes
articles.summary: Sony is shutting down Bluepoint Games, the PlayStation studio behind well-received remakes like Shadow of the Colossus and Demon’s Souls. Sony purchased it in 2021.
articles.body: Sony is shutting down Bluepoint Games, the PlayStation studio behind well-received remakes of games like Shadow of the Colossus and Demon’s Souls, according to Bloomberg. The change was made “following a recent business review,” a spokesperson told the publication. About 70 staffers will be cut, and the studio will shut down in March. “Bluepoint Games is an incredibly talented team and their technical expertise has delivered exceptional experiences for the PlayStation community,” a spokesperson told Bloomberg. “We thank them for their passion, creativity and craftmanship.” Sony didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment. Sony acquired Bluepoint Games in 2021 following a string of successful updates to many PlayStation franchises, including remasters of the first three Uncharted titles and of Gravity Rush. But after Sony’s purchase, the company appears to have set the studio on a different course than the remakes and remasters that made it a powerhouse: it co-developed 2022’s God of War: Ragnarok, then spent years working on an unannounced live service God of War game that Sony canceled in January. Bluepoint is just the latest PlayStation studio affected by major changes in recent years. Sony closed down Concord developer Firewalk Studios in 2024 shortly after the game’s disastrous launch. At that same time, it announced the shutdown of mobile studio Neon Koi, too. In 2024, Bungie also laid off 220 employees and moved others into Sony Interactive Entertainment.

articles.title: Xbox is closing down Hellblade creator Ninja Theory
articles.summary: Xbox is closing down Ninja Theory, the studio behind the Hellblade series, a source tells The Verge. Staffers were told on a call on Monday about the closure.
articles.body: Xbox is closing down Ninja Theory, the studio behind the Hellblade series, a source tells The Verge. Staffers were told on a call on Monday about the closure, but they are hoping the studio will find a buyer. The closure comes as “several” Xbox studios at Microsoft, including Compulsion Games and Double Fine, are in “active negotiations” about spinning off, Bloomberg reports. The closure and negotiations follow Xbox CEO Asha Sharma and chief content officer Matt Booty warning last week of a “reset” at Xbox, laying out several challenges facing Xbox’s business — including that it had “over extended” with its studio system and the hardware component crisis is significantly driving up prices. Kotaku reported earlier on Monday that Microsoft was planning to shut down Compulsion, though it noted in an update that studio leadership was in “negotiations” with Microsoft. Sharma has made many major decisions since taking over at Xbox in February, including locking down Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution as Xbox console exclusives in an announcement at its Xbox Games Showcase just over a week ago. During that event, Microsoft also revealed a new Hellblade game, Senua, and its future with this change is unclear. Xbox didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.

articles.title: Netflix is closing two game studios
articles.summary: Netflix plans to shut down Night School Studio and Moonloot Games. It’s also cutting staff from its games business.
articles.body: Netflix plans to shut down two of its gaming studios, as reported by Game File and Variety, as it makes a bigger shift toward party games and titles streamed to TVs. One of the studios being shut down is Night School Studio, creators of the Oxenfree series. Netflix bought Night School in 2021, and it just released a horror experience called Unhinged for TVs and launched a mobile game in 2025 tied to Black Mirror. The other studio that’s set to close is Helsinki-based Moonloot Games, which was created in 2022. Netflix’s big push into TV-based games kicked off late last year and was a pivot from a mobile-focused approach that featured prestige indie titles. But Netflix has let many of those indie hits leave its mobile lineup as it focuses instead on four pillars of kids, party, narrative, and “mainstream” games. “As we continue to prioritize these areas, we see an opportunity to be more focused in our execution, so we are making organizational changes to the business to match those priorities,” Netflix spokesperson Chrissy Kelleher tells The Verge. Netflix is also eliminating “some” additional roles in its games business, according to Kelleher. The cuts include Tara Voelker, who says she was the “single accessibility person” on the gaming team. Last year, Netflix shut down the studio behind a Squid Game mobile title and sold Cozy Grove studio Spry Fox back to its original owners. In 2024, Netflix closed down a AAA studio that never released a game.

Marroncream is one of the most mysterious residents of Friendship Island. A fashionable rabbit with a French accent, she was introduced to Hello Kitty Island Adventure as part of the Welcome Home update . articles.title: Phantom Blade Zero Sells 4 Million Copies in 72 Hours
articles.summary: Phantom Blade Zero is officially the next big thing. Developer S-Game has announced that its wuxia-themed action game has surpassed a significant milestone in just a few days.
articles.body:
Phantom Blade Zero is officially the next big thing. Developer S-Game has announced that its wuxia-themed action game has surpassed a significant milestone in just a few days.

Within 72 hours of going on sale, Phantom Blade Zero has sold 4 million copies. The official X / Twitter account posted the news with a message: “Thank you everyone from the bottom of our hearts for all the love and support!”

Even on its first day, it was clear this was going to be a beast. Phantom Blade Zero was ahead of Steam’s biggest games , from PUBG to Dota 2, topping the Steam charts as soon as it launched. It was also the best-selling game on Steam by revenue, ahead of Modern Warfare 4, Aion 2, and Probably Stolen, a Cyberpunk shopkeeper sim that's going viral. Steam concurrents peaked on Sunday with a whopping 833,921 players.

Phantom Blade Zero - Donnie Yen Behind the Scenes Photos

The early success shouldn't come as a huge surprise. Last week, it was estimated that Phantom Blade Zero had sold over 1 million copies before launch across launch platforms Steam and PS5, and Tencent’s WeGame (an online PC storefront in China). Nearly two thirds of total prelaunch sales were from China, Taiwan, or Hong Kong.

IGN's Phantom Blade Zero review returned a 9/10. We said: "Phantom Blade Zero is an unbelievably smooth action game filled with memorable boss fights, compelling combat, and limitless swagger."

Phantom Blade Zero is a monster hit, but it's not quite on par with Black Myth: Wukong, which managed 10 million sales in the first three days .

Roger Craig Smith — best known as Sonic the Hedgehog, Ezio Auditore, Batman, and Chris Redfield — plays the lead character. The actor is joined by Mu Xiaokui actor Maggie Robertson, who played Lady Dimitrescu in Resident Evil 7. Elsewhere in the cast, Donnie Yen served as a key creative consultant and stars as the character Mó Yuan (Soul's father) through full facial, voice, and motion capture.

Before you step into the Phantom World, we’ve put together a helpful list of Things Phantom Blade Zero Doesn’t Tell You . We’ve also got a step-by-step Phantom Blade Zero Walkthrough in progress, plus guides for the game’s Weapons , Accessories , and Phantom Edges .

articles.title: Speedrunner Breaks Super Mario Bros. World Record While Dressed as the Italian Plumber, Now Just 2 Frames From Theoretical Perfect Run
articles.summary: Niftski, the speedrunning world record holder for Super Mario Bros., beat his own record on a Halloween livestream while dressed as Mario. Speaking in character, he said: “Hopefully I don’t get this today because that would be very stupid.” Guess what?
articles.body:
Niftski, the speedrunning world record holder for Super Mario Bros., beat his own record on a Halloween livestream while dressed as Mario. Speaking in character, he said: “Hopefully I don’t get this today because that would be very stupid.” Guess what?

This Halloween run, which you can watch on Niftski's YouTube channel , shaved 0.33 seconds off the previous world record, also held by Niftski — two frames away from a perfect run.

4:54.299 SMB1 ANY% WORLD RECORD ON HALLOWEEN WHILE LARPING AS MARIO! It doesn't even feel real that I actually achieved this, but here we are. Only 2 frames (33 milliseconds) stand between this run and absolute perfection / TAS tie. 4:54.265 next! — Niftski (@Niftski) November 1, 2026

4:54.299 SMB1 ANY% WORLD RECORD ON HALLOWEEN WHILE LARPING AS MARIO! It doesn't even feel real that I actually achieved this, but here we are. Only 2 frames (33 milliseconds) stand between this run and absolute perfection / TAS tie. 4:54.265 next!

According to Niftski, those two frames were lost early in the run and kept him away from a “perfect run,” theorized to be the absolute pinnacle of Super Mario Bros. “any percent” attempts. He messed up fast accelerations in the first and second rooms by a small amount which cost one frame each.

If it is accurate and there are no more strats to bring the time down significantly, that just leaves the run and those two frames. That means there’s only two milliseconds left, which means there are only two more world records possible in the category.

“Will this be like the first ever game perfected? Like what's gonna happen once someone matches the TAS? It's just over?” asked one fan .

Niftski breaks the SMB1 world record while doing the worst Mario impression ever. Frame-perfect hands, not-so-perfect voice 🍄 — imngrok • Stream Clips (@imngrok) November 1, 2026

Niftski breaks the SMB1 world record while doing the worst Mario impression ever. Frame-perfect hands, not-so-perfect voice 🍄

Niftski sits alone at the top of the speedrunning records, and it seems the only person who can beat him is himself, dressed as Mario. He holds the records for warpless, glitchless, and the “any percent” category, which is a race to the end by any means necessary, skipping whatever you can using exploits and glitches.

It’s that last category he beat this Halloween, taking his previous record of 4:54:332 down to 4:54:229 — that’s minutes, seconds, and milliseconds. About halfway through the run, he committed fully to Mario and let Nintendo fill his heart.

According to the speedrunner, being a doofus and pretending to be Mario helped. “It made me not nervous at all,” said Niftski, “it doesn’t even feel real. It felt so casual.”

“I can't believe I witnessed a russian mario do the 67 and get any% wr in the same video,” said one X / Twitter user who watched the stream.

articles.title: Elon Musk Joins Growing Backlash Over OpenAI Sam Altman's RAM Comments
articles.summary: Elon Musk has joined the growing backlash over OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's recent comments on RAM.
articles.body:
Elon Musk has joined the growing backlash over Sam Altman’s recent comments on RAM.

Last week, the OpenAI CEO sparked outrage across the internet and, specifically, within the gamer community, when he said he thought it was “terrible” for people to have RAM in their PCs rather than a data center .

In an interview with YouTuber Cheeky Pint , Altman said: "From a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer, and being used 5% of the time. Like, you want maximum utilization in the cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply constrained environment. And somehow many people's intuition is the opposite of that."

The comments have been widely ridiculed, with many suggesting that, whether he intended it or not, Altman sounds like he wants to take away personal ownership of memory and force society to use resources for the benefit of AI companies such as his. Social media was flooded with posts, images, and videos of people slamming Altman for the suggestion, promising to protect their precious memory from any who might try to claim it. Others have simply dunked on Altman for the comments, with countless memes and, yes, AI-generated videos showing the AI billionaire in various states of embarrassment.

Here’s 576GB worth of go f*ck yourself Sam Altman

Using a stick of RAM to stir my coffee this morning, fuck you, Sam Altman — Sick (@sickdotdev) November 1, 2026

Using a stick of RAM to stir my coffee this morning, fuck you, Sam Altman

sam altman: your ram should be in data centers me with 32 gigs of ram: — Micky D (@DeMickyD) October 31, 2026

sam altman: your ram should be in data centers me with 32 gigs of ram:

Found on reddit. Hilarious — wayward strategy (@waywardstrategy) November 1, 2026

Speaking of AI billionaires, his tech rival, Elon Musk, got in on the act with a meme of his own, letting his millions of followers know where he stands on the subject of memory ownership.

"The people deserve to have their RAM too!" Musk declared in a post on X, the social media platform he owns, alongside a meme of Colonel Hans Landa from Quentin Tarantino’s 2009 film Inglourious Basterds.

The people deserve to have their RAM too! — Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 1, 2026

The people deserve to have their RAM too!

The AI boom has led to a scarcity of memory to power it, which in turn has caused graphics cards, video game consoles, and PC components to skyrocket in price. Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have all raised the prices of their consoles as a result of the ‘RAMpocalypse,’ while the RTX 5080 just disappeared off of Nvidia's marketplace, weeks after the RTX 5090 was all but discontinued.

Microsoft reportedly expects its next-gen Xbox, codenamed Project Helix, to cost as much as $1,800 . Sony has yet to announce its next-gen hardware, but analysts suspect it will push back its launch for as long as possible amid cost concern.

Altman, though, is unlikely to change his line of thinking any time soon. He’s currently on the hunt for up to $20 billion in a new funding round co-led by UAE investors, down from an earlier target of about $30 billion, according to CNBC .

While Musk is happy to take shots at Altman, he’s having AI problems of his own. In a remarkable tweet , the Tesla and SpaceX owner appeared to admit to throttling Grok Bot for being “unsustainably” expensive. Users had complained there were hitting limits sooner than expected, and Musk replied to one such complaint to say the cost of running the AI agent was “unsustainably high relative to revenue.”

This in turn sparked an explosion of comments across social media, with many suggesting Musk's admission here signalled a significant issue with the economics of generative AI itself. Grok Bot, launched in beta in August with paid weekly active users nearing 800,000 by late October. The agent runs autonomous tasks on virtual computers, demanding far more compute than simple chatbots. Heavy users faced sudden lockouts and frustration, with some canceling plans.

In a follow-up tweet replying to one person highlighting the potential impact of Musk's statement, he said: "Just being sensible."

articles.title: Google Has a Cool The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Easter Egg That Transports Us Back to the 1998 Era of Search Results
articles.summary: Google just got a The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Easter egg that transports you back to the 1998 version of the search engine — complete with blue links for results.
articles.body:
Google just got a The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Easter egg that transports you back to the 1998 version of the search engine — complete with blue links for results.

The remake of the Nintendo 64 classic comes out this Thursday, November 5, but you can find the secret on Google now if you type “zelda” into the search bar and press enter. This makes the Master Sword appear in the bottom-right corner of the screen.

Click the Master Sword and it gets shoved into its pedestal, an audio effect plays, and the screen distorts to pull you through time. Now you’re back at the old, useful, minimalist Google that showed search results as a series of blue links for people to click on.

What you’re seeing is Google from 1998, the year the original Ocarina of Time launched. It was the year of the Saving Private Ryan movie, the rise of teen pop icons like Britney Spears and breakthrough television shows like Sex and the City. The Boy Is Mine by Brandy and Monica would have been blasting from the stereos of passing cars, kids would have been playing with Furbys, and everyone was rocking a Nokia. Ah, nostalgia. Google’s 1998 version even has the “I’m feeling lucky” option, which would just take you to a random search result.

As Nintendo has pulled back the curtain on The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake , we’ve begun to get a better understanding of how this Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive will look and feel to play. IGN has already got you covered with an extensive hands-on preview , as well as a roundup of all the changes we’ve noticed so far compared to the N64 masterpiece.

While you wait, check out a special episode of Nintendo Voice Chat where we dive deeper into our Zelda preview. Meanwhile, Eiji Aonuma, producer of the Zelda series at Nintendo, recently admitted some of the younger members of his team had never played the original game , but insisted that was very much a good thing for the development of the remake.

articles.title: Dune Messiah: Book 1 Adapts Frank Herbert’s Sci-Fi Epic to Comics
articles.summary: Just in time for the theatrical release of Dune: Part Three, Abrams ComicArts is releasing an ambitious adaptation of Frank Herbert's legendary novel Dune Messiah.
articles.body:
If you want a taste of what's coming in director Denis Villeneuve's third and final Dune film, you need to read Frank Herbert's 1969 novel, Dune Messiah. Luckily, there's a new option for interested Dune fans, as Abrams ComicArts is continuing its line of Dune graphic novels with the first of two Dune Messiah adaptations.

Ahead of its November 3 release, IGN can exclusively reveal a new preview of Dune Messiah: Book 1. Check it out in the slideshow gallery below:

Dune Messiah: Book 1 Graphic Novel Preview Gallery

Dune Messiah: Book 1 is adapted by Kevin J. Anderson and Brian Herbert, with art by Michael Shelfer and a cover by Bill Sienkiewicz. Here's the official summary of the book:

In Dune Messiah: Book 1, Paul Atreides is now Emperor of the known universe, but absolute power has made him both a ruler and a target. Revered as a messianic figure by the Fremen and feared by rival houses, Paul must confront a growing conspiracy that threatens to unravel his reign. As political enemies close in and his prophetic visions begin to shift, the future of his empire—and the people he loves—hangs in the balance. Perfect for fans of the Dune films, longtime readers of the novels, and newcomers alike, this adaptation offers a unique view of the saga's darker second act.

A visually stunning graphic novel adaptation of Frank Herbert's Dune Messiah, this volume brings one of science fiction's most pivotal stories to life in a bold, immersive new format. Rich, detailed artwork captures the scale of Arrakis and the complexity of its characters, while the visual format sharpens the story's core tensions—power, religion, and destiny—with new immediacy.

“Dune Messiah, Frank Herbert’s sequel to Dune, was a surprise to readers in its tone and message and how the great hero Paul Atreides falls to corruption and treachery,” said Anderson in a statement. “In interpreting this story in a faithful, scene-by-scene graphic novel, we focused on the scope of the vast landscapes, the color of the culture, and the characters struggling with forces beyond their control. Michael Shelfer’s art makes the story expansive and a delight for the reader’s eye."

Dune Messiah: Book 1 will be released on November 3, with Book 2 to follow in 2027. You can preorder a copy on Amazon .

Dune: Part Three hits theaters on December 18, 2026 , a day movie lovers have crowned "Dunesday." But if the latest trailer is any indication, Part Three may diverge from the plot of Dune Messiah more than fans are expecting.

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

The Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is set to release this Thursday, November 5. The first batch of physical copies of the game includes a textured foil cover – but these will only be available while supplies last.

That day has come at Amazon ; the retailer sold through its supply of textured-foil-cover copies over the weekend. Thankfully, if you haven’t preordered it yet and you want a copy with a reflective cover, you can still preorder it at a few retailers ( see it at Walmart ).

The textured foil on the cover creates a sparkling reflection effect when you rotate the game case in the light. You can see what it looks like up close in Nintendo's Instagram post below.

Amazon’s listing for the Ocarina of Time remake has a note saying it will be “available again starting Nov. 5,” but I’m fairly certain the new stock will have a standard, non-textured, non-foil cover.

articles.title: World of Warcraft Forever Preload and Global Release Times Confirmed
articles.summary: World of Warcraft Forever is just a few days away, and Blizzard has confirmed the global release times and preload details. Here's when you can play in your timezone.
articles.body:
World of Warcraft Forever is just a few days away, and Blizzard has confirmed the global release times and preload details.

WoW Forever launches on November 4, and has a global release scheduled, which means everyone will be able to start playing at the same time, no matter where they are. This is super important in an MMO like WoW, because it means that one region isn't able to get significantly further ahead than any other.

World of Warcraft Forever Global Release Times

Because World of Warcraft Forever has a global release, all you really have to do is look at its official release time of 3pm PST and convert that to your own timezone. However, because of the nature of a global release, depending on where you are in the world, the game will either be launching on November 4 or on November 5.

World of Warcraft Forever Preload Details

World of Warcraft Forever is available to preload now. Simply open or download the Battle.net launcher, then WoW Forever should show up in the 'Favorites' bar by default. If it doesn't, go to 'Games' and then search for 'World of Warcraft.' Then, click the WoW icon, go to 'game version' and ensure 'WoW Forever' is selected, and then hit the big blue 'Install' button.

Once it's downloaded you'll be good to log in when the servers go live on November 4 at 3pm PST.

How Much Space Will You Need For World of Warcraft Forever?

According to Blizzard's system requirements, World of Warcraft Forever will need at least 128GB of available space, but I'd actually reserve a bit extra. Just like any version of WoW, there are going to be hundreds of mods available from day one, and unless you're looking to play the game entirely with the default UI, you're going to want to make sure you have some space for add-ons. I'd recommend having at least 150GB reserved for Forever, just in case. Note, as well, that Blizzard specifically calls out an SSD, rather than a harddrive.

World of Warcraft Forever minimum PC requirements:

CPU: ' 4 cores, 3GHz processor (Intel Haswell or Ryzen Zen)' – think Intel Core i5 4460 / AMD Ryzen 5 1600X

GPU: 'DirectX 12 Capable 4GB GPU, GTX 10-series or RDNA 1' – Think Nvidia GeForce GTX 1060 / AMD Radeon RX 5600

World of Warcraft Forever recommended PC requirements:

CPU: '8 performance cores, 5.2GHz boost clock; Intel Core Ultra (series 2) or AMD Ryzen Zen 5' – think Intel Core Ultra 5 265K / AMD Ryzen 5 9600X

GPU: 'DirectX 12 capable 8GB GPU; Nvidia RTX 40 series/AMD RDNA 3/Intel Arc B-Series' – think Nvidia GeForce RTX 4060 / AMD Radeon RX 7600 / Intel Arc B570

While you wait to play, be sure to check out our big interview with Blizzard on its plans for World of Warcraft: Forever post-launch, which include update frequency and new locations.

articles.title: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered Is a Delightful Throwback Brawler From a Bygone Era of Lazy Weekends - Review
articles.summary: A delightful throwback to a bygone era of lazy weekends past.
articles.body:
The first time I ever saw Japan's most famous kaiju on the big screen was in Godzilla 2000: Millennium. Like any nine-year-old kid, I was obsessed with Big G. I read the Dark Horse comics, and I taped all the movies I could on TV. Things were different then; Godzilla was a big deal, but theatrical releases for Godzilla films were incredibly rare in the States If you saw those movies, it was on TV and they were dubbed or edited versions released under different titles like Godzilla: King of the Monsters or Godzilla vs. The Sea Monster. After Godzilla 2000 underperformed, it took another five years for the series to see a theatrical release in the U.S. – and into that void stomped 2002’s Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee.

It was the perfect mix of subject matter (big monsters who were super into professional wrestling), genre (3D fighting game), and time period (licensed games were still, like… a thing). It was the kind of game that could dominate a pizza-filled sleepover weekend or become your personality for an entire summer. One friend’s parents bought it for them, and that copy became communal: a holy thing, carried from place to place. Maybe it’s fitting that it’s back now in the form of Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered, 24 years later. The world (and Godzilla) has changed a lot, but original developer Pipeworks is still at the helm. It somehow feels just as relevant now as it did then, just in different ways, and revisiting it was a joy even removed from the nostalgia.

There is no one-to-one equivalent for what Destroy All Monsters Melee is, but the idea is pretty simple: you pick one of 12 monsters from Godzilla’s history (up through Godzilla 2000) – Godzilla, Gigan, Megalon, Ghidorah, etc. – then choose a real-world city or iconic Godzilla location to battle it out in. You’ll fight in classic rubber suit wrestling style while dodging environmental hazards, knocking down buildings, throwing rocks and skyscrapers at each other, and squashing the annoying military forces that really would prefer if you made a mess somewhere else. Last kaiju standing wins.

Despite the name, this isn't a straight remaster. You're not just looking at uprezzed models. It looks fantastic while also maintaining the “these are guys in rubber suits drop-kicking each other” vibe that defines the films it’s based on. The audio pulls its weight, too – the soundtrack has the booming authority you'd expect from a Godzilla film, buildings crumble and collapse spectacularly, beam attacks sound powerful and painful, the radio calls from military forces in the area let you know where they’ll be focusing their fire, and the announcer is having a blast. And the monsters, of course, sound like themselves. And yeah, Godzilla makes The Noise, just like you remember, even if it’s your first time here.

All of this is held together by a spit-and-duct-tape story that's just there to get you brawling: see, there's this alien race called the Vortaak. They're little green men with funky helmets, straight-from-the-‘50s fashion sense, flying saucers, and more than a little ego. They're here to take over the Earth, and what better way to do it than mind control the frankly absurd number of kaiju that are just hanging around, ready to smash a city at a moment's notice? Unfortunately for them, whichever Monster you pick breaks free of their mind control and decides the Earth is worth saving. Driving off the Vortaak means KOing the other monsters. All in a day's work, really.

That's Adventure mode, which is one of several single-player options for you to rearrange cities in. You've also got Destruction for the score chasers, where you have to wreck a city in a time limit, a souped-up Adventure mode for monsters who are at a higher level and have better stats (which you gain from experience you earn as you play certain modes), and Survival, which is exactly what it sounds like.

Listen, you can count the number of fighting games with good single-player modes on two hands (and several of those have the words “Soul Calibur” in their titles), but what's on offer here is solid if not spectacular. You only start with four monsters and a few stages unlocked, but Pipeworks has smartly reworked this remaster so you can unlock the rest in pretty much whatever order you like. You just have to meet the requirements, which you do by playing, following rumors, and unlocking research, and you can swap what you're focusing on whenever you like.

On the one hand, yeah, it's super satisfying to unlock Ghidorah because it's Ghidorah – as soon as he stops being a silhouette I can't select and starts being a gloriously golden three-headed dragon I can take into battle, some lizard part of my brain gets very happy because I can't wait to fly around and shoot lightning with that sumbitch. On the other hand, it's mad annoying to see Rodan or Ghidorah or Mecha Godzilla in Adventure mode and have the 12-year-old who lives in my head put down his slice of pizza long enough to be like “hell yeah, I wanna play that one” and then realize I can't, especially in multiplayer. Does it give you more reasons to keep playing? Absolutely, and this stuff was part and parcel of the original experience. But man, sometimes you just wanna throw down with your friends without worrying about unlocks, you know?

Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered Screenshots

Multiplayer, of course, is really what Destroy All Monsters Melee is designed for, and I'm so happy that Pipeworks has added online play in addition to the returning local options. It even works really well! Most of the matches I played pre-release were smooth, though I did suffer a few disconnects. (Almost all of which happened when I was winning or doing well – I'm not saying my boy Lucas is a fraud or anything, but…)

It's here, in the multiplayer, that Destroy All Monsters Melee really shines. People will tell you, naively, that this is a button masher with no depth. These people are foolish and wrong, and if this were a Godzilla movie, they'd got a dramatic close-up shot right before a giant monster foot turned them into paste. Can you play a chaotic four-player free-for-all where everybody is mashing? Sure. You can also do wacky team battles or square off against the never-as-challenging-as-another-person CPU (though, bafflingly, you can't mix CPU opponents with friends online; let me do a comp stomp, man!). This can certainly be a casual party game if you want it to be.

But the thing about Destroy All Monsters Melee is that there is actually quite a bit more to it. Each monster has punch, kick, and fierce attacks that you can string into combos. Tilt the left stick in a direction and you get heavy attacks. Every kaiju has an energy attack governed by an energy bar that you can use as a quick projectile or charge for a beam. You can also pick up and throw buildings and rocks, or even other kaiju. You can run, jump, fly (if your character has wings), crouch, and block.

All of this opens up most of the stuff you'd see in a traditional fighting game. Someone shoot a projectile at you? Duck it. If you've knocked another monster down, they can wake up with an attack, but if you block it or stand just outside of their range, you can punish them instead. Finishing a predictable string when an opponent is blocking means you are either getting hit or thrown for your trouble.

Every monster also has different stats to account for. Gigan's sword arms mean he hits… well, like a kaiju with sword arms, but his projectiles are relatively weak. Anguirus can't block normally, but his spiked shell means anyone who hits him while his back is turned is gonna be dancing around in a lot of pain. Megalon can burrow and come up under you. And Godzilla 2000's additional bit of quickness means he can apply pressure a lot more easily than his ‘90s counterpart. Knowing what the other city smasher you're staring down can do matters, and someone who understands the difference between Blunt and Edge attacks or who knows when to duck your strings is going to beat your colossal ass up and down Tokyo Bay if you're just mashing.

But smart map play matters, too. Once you start to destroy a city, there's less cover to hide behind in future rounds and fewer things to throw at your opponent. It also means it’s easier to make a beeline for the power-ups that drop on the map – like Rage, which buffs your character and provides access to powerful Rage attacks. There are health and energy boosts, as well as my personal favorite, the Mothra Airstrike, which the announcer proclaims with a relish that makes me think he's been waiting to see a giant moth divebomb another kaiju his whole life. If you break down cliffs on Monster Island, you can chuck another monster into the lava. Crack open the forcefield on the alien’s Mothership and there's a whole other part of the stage to fight in. It's good stuff.

Is it as deep as Street Fighter or Guilty Gear of Tekken? No. But a lot goes into a match of Destroy All Monsters Melee, and knowing your kaiju goes a long way. There is replay value in filling out the gallery and score chasing in Destruction Mode, but if you vibe with what's here, it will be because you love it. And by “it,” I mean uppercutting a monster the size of the Chrysler Building and watching him hang in the air for a second before he comes crashing back down to Earth.

Admittedly, the deeper stuff isn't easy to learn because Destroy All Monsters Melee barely teaches you any of it. Aside from loading screen text and a basic movelist, there is no tutorial of any kind, so I learned by trial and error, talking to the people I was playing with, and hunting down guides for the original game. That sucks, because the fun part is digging into these systems, and it's much more fun when you understand the layers hidden beneath the scales (or metal).

I came out of Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered with my brain rewired – or maybe more accurately, it reminded me of what's important. It's not how big the roster is or whether there's a progression system to keep you playing forever once the character unlocks run out. It’s not about achievements or daily quests or a battle pass or all the other useless Skinner Box nonsense crammed into everything these days. This is a time capsule, a pure reminder that what makes a game are the moments at 2 a.m. when you throw your buddy into the lava pit… which happens to have a Rage power up in it. It's the comebacks and the laughs. It's like stepping back into the shoes of my nine-year-old self, seeing a Godzilla film in theaters before the series was drowning in cultural clout and an interconnected multimedia universe. The joy is in the thing itself. In surrendering your expectations and remembering how things can make you feel if you let them. Everything else is noise. And not the cool Godzilla kind.

articles.title: Xbox’s former COO has ‘serious concerns’ about her abrupt departure
articles.summary: Former Xbox chief operating officer Helen Chiang is setting the record straight on her sudden Microsoft departure.
articles.body: Xbox’s former chief operating officer, Helen Chiang, suddenly left Microsoft less than two weeks ago after being promoted into the role in July. I wrote in my Notepad newsletter last week that it seemed very weird for Chiang to suddenly depart Microsoft after 21 years with a surprisingly short memo from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. Now, Chiang says she has “serious concerns” about how she was treated. In a lengthy LinkedIn post — entitled “Clarity is Kindness,” a reference to Sharma’s WSJ profile — Chiang doesn’t dispute that she was fired, but she doesn’t say why she was let go. Eurogamer reported last month that Chiang had been “terminated for policy violations,” but she says this is “not accurate.” Chiang denies unfounded rumors that speculated she was leaking confidential information, or that she left to join a competitor. It’s clear the decision to leave Xbox was out of her hands. “You don’t spend two decades somewhere without developing a deep loyalty to the people, teams, and businesses you’ve helped build,” says Chiang. “Xbox was never just another stop in my career. My end game was always to keep building here.” She also denies engaging in “discrimination, bullying, harassment, insider trading, embezzlement, or other fraudulent activity.” Like I wrote in Notepad last week, Chiang has been described to me by multiple Xbox employees as highly respected, with high integrity. “I stand by my record: both the results I delivered and the way I have treated people throughout my career,” says Chiang. The most significant part of Chiang’s post is a paragraph on fairness and accountability, hinting that she wasn’t treated fairly: > I believe in fairness, accountability, and holding ourselves to the standards we expect of others. Those standards only mean something when they’re applied consistently. I have serious concerns about how they were applied in my case, and I believe those concerns deserve to be taken seriously. Chiang also says “This is not how I ever imagined my story here would end. And it is not the whole story.” We’ve reached out to Chiang to ask if she’s pursuing legal action against Microsoft. We’ve also asked Microsoft to comment on Chiang’s post, but the company didn’t respond in time for publication.

articles.title: All Banyan Heart Locations - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: There are five total Banyan Hearts in Phantom Blade 0 that you'll need to collect. Banyan Hearts are found in five different locations around the world,
articles.body:
There are five total Banyan Hearts in Phantom Blade 0 that you'll need to collect. Banyan Hearts are found in five different locations around the world, and every time you find one of these trees, you'll need to complete a combat gauntlet to obtain the heart. Below you'll find the location of all five Banyan Hearts in Phantom Blade 0.

The first Banyan Heart you'll need to grab is in the Crimson Forest, just south of the Parting Mists Bell. Upon reaching that bell, drop down directly in front of you toward the water. You'll see a large tree looming in the distance; approach it to begin the trial.

The next Banyan Heart you'll have access to is in Pangzhen. Just left of the Green Serpent House Bell, you'll fight You Loong in shallow water. Upon defeating You Loong, you'll gain access to a small wooden bridge at the back of this combat arena. Follow the path to reach the next Banyan Tree, and complete the next fight to obtain the Banyan Heart.

Mandate Encampment Banyan Heart Location

The third Banyan Heart location is at the Mandate Encampment, which you'll gain access to as you progress through Pangzhen. Upon arriving at the Mandate Encampment, look to your right, and you'll see an anchor point for the Hunter's Chain Sickle; use it to put yourself right in front of the Banyan Tree.

When you arrive in Meigu Lake, take the boat just a bit to the right to find the Banyan Tree on its own island. As you've done previously, take on the combat trial and defeat it to claim the fourth Banyan Heart.

Mountain of Imprisonment Banyan Heart Location

The fifth and final Banyan Heart location is found at the Shrine Outer Gate Bell in the Mountain of Imprisonment. From here, go across the rickety wooden bridges to find the Banyan Tree.

After grabbing the final Banyan Heart from this tree, you will have everything you need to finish out the skills in your skill tree (granted you've also purchased the Banyan Hearts from Quick hand Zhang).

You'll also complete the Tale Heart of the Banyan.

For more Phantom Blade 0 tips and tricks, be sure to check out our full walkthrough of the game, as well as our side quests list so you don't miss a thing.

articles.title: Alien: Isolation 2 Devs Tease New Protagonist, Planet Setting, and 1979 Film Roots
articles.summary: IGN sat down with Creative Director Al Hope and Project Art Director Ana Sopikova to discuss why Alien: Isolation 2 took so long, how Ridley Scott's original 1979 movie continues to shape the game's design, and what fans can expect from this long-awaited return.
articles.body:
It's been 12 years since Alien: Isolation first introduced us to the unique terror of being trapped with a Xenomorph, and now Creative Assembly is finally ready to drag us kicking and screaming back into its nightmare. With Alien: Isolation 2 set for release next year, the studio is returning to the survival horror roots that made the original such a cult classic, but this time with a new protagonist, a new location, and plenty of fresh opportunities to be horribly murdered by everyone's favorite acid-blooded nightmare.

At the Lucca Comics and Games Festival, IGN sat down with Creative Director Al Hope and Project Art Director Ana Sopikova to discuss why the sequel took so long, how Ridley Scott's original 1979 movie continues to shape the game's design, and what fans can expect from this long-awaited return. We also talked Alien canon, Amanda Ripley's role, and whether there's already an Alien: Isolation 3 lurking somewhere in Hope's imagination.

IGN: The first Alien movie was a horror movie, and then they moved on to action and other genres. Both of the Alien Isolation games are survival horror games. Was there ever any idea of making Alien Isolation 2 in a different genre?

Al Hope: No, it's a short answer to that. I guess we absolutely adore that first movie and, obviously, Isolation, but we feel like there's still so much to mine or tap into in the universe of that first movie. And it felt like we wanted to tell other stories in the same part of that space of the universe in the same kind of context. So yeah, no, I guess we feel like in Alien Isolation 2, I think the promise is about transporting you back to that time and place, that window of the timeline where just one alien can be absolutely terrifying and an incredible challenge, an incredible experience. And I suppose if you just wanted to explore that, go back and explore that and evolve it.

IGN: The Xenomorph is a very iconic monster character. Is it challenging designing a Xenomorph for this game that is part of this iconic kind of legacy?

Ana Sopikova: Well, of course. It's a great honor I think for all of us and especially for our team to just be able to contribute to such an iconic IP. I think to go back to what Al was saying, we are really staying true to Ridley Scott’s original 1979 film, and we have a really good close relationship with 20th Century [Studios]. We have an archive with just loads of behind-the-scenes photos from the set, just really close-up images that really allow the team to just go deep in there and study and look at the types of materials they used at the time and look at the types of methods that they were using for building this costume. And then we've just taken that and applied it to what we are doing for the game. And I think really in terms of designing, we are staying true to 1979.

So we're definitely not reinventing the wheel there. And fictionally, obviously in Isolation 2, as people might have seen from the trailer, they have recognized the Haz Lab. So it is the same creature that you encountered in the first game that landed on this new planet. So you can imagine it will be quite similar to what people have seen before, but we're still taking it a little bit further just again in terms of fidelity. Time has passed, there's new technology, and we can just afford a little bit more detail, a little bit of a shinier texture to put it safely. So yeah, there's still space for us to go deeper, but we're not deviating madly elsewhere because for us, really, 1979 is the focus.

IGN: Speaking of the movies, how did it feel to see the emergency phone save points from Alien: Isolation appear as a special Easter egg in Fede Álvarez's Alien: Romulus?

Al Hope: Just thinking about what you were saying there, I think the team feels really privileged to be in this space, and obviously we were absolutely blown away and thrilled when Fede Álvarez put the save station in Romulus.

I think that's the privilege. We get to work with this original source material and we have the potential to, we're helping grow it. And that is, I think, for all of us, such a privilege and so exciting, as well.

IGN: So just so I understand, because I know there was a lot spoken about that, what you just mentioned about what Fede Álvarez did. And so it's safe to assume that both of these games now kind of exist in the official canon of the Alien universe?

Al Hope: It's really ultimately for the fans [to decide]. I think they really embraced the first game, and I think that's what's important. Sure, there are timelines and all that stuff. That's cool. I think we're just really focused on trying to tell that next chapter.

IGN: Going in a different direction, obviously Amanda is in this game in some capacity. Can you speak to that at all?

Al Hope: Well, we're really proud of Amanda, but to be clear, you're playing as a new character in Isolation 2. And that felt like the natural choice for us. We wanted to tell a new story. It felt like the right way to do that would be in a new location, and being in a new location, then actually seeing it through the eyes of a new character, seemed to make a lot of sense for us. And a character that has a different perspective. She works for the company; she hasn't encountered the creature before. And so yeah, I guess we're super excited about Blake.

IGN: With the first game, one of the most popular mods was the VHS color filter. I don't want to spoil anything, but is there a chance that it makes some sort of official appearance in this game, or is that just a cool community thing that was the first game?

Ana Sopikova: Who knows? I mean, it was still quite early, so I'm not going to comment specifically. There will be a photo mode. I think we've just confirmed it in the Q&A recently. We spent actually a lot of time researching cameras and camera technology and looking at it through the lens of lo-fi sci-fi and just really being authentic to the tech and to the actual, I guess, the physical objects and physical technology. So we are viewing the photo mode through that lens. So who knows?

I think there's definitely going to be plenty of opportunities for fans to capture and express themselves.

IGN: Going back to the first game and the process, so it's been, what is it, 12 years since the first game. Why now? I guess just why now? Why is now the time to have a sequel to the original game?

Al Hope: Yeah, that's a good question. So I've been thinking about what we could do for a sequel before we'd actually released the first game. But I guess as a studio, we were busy, and I guess what we've benefited from is that decade of new players discovering the game and getting their feedback. And the short answer is it felt like the time was right to come back. And so yeah, just super thrilled to be having this opportunity with this really fantastic team, which is great because the team is this mix of people who worked on the first game, and then we've got really fantastic fresh new talent, new talent coming on board. So it's this really lovely combination.

Ana Sopikova: There are just so many fans on the team, and for so many people, it's the absolute dream project. They grew up as fans of the game, and now they finally have the opportunity to come and actually contribute to the sequel. So they just bring this next level of energy and passion, and it's great.

IGN: Is there one thing that comes to mind that is the most difficult part of the design process, especially when you are going back to look at an original that is a classic?

Ana Sopikova: I wouldn't use the word difficult. Obviously there are creative challenges. Obviously for us, because we are on the planet, and we are laser-focused on the first film that took place in space, apart from a very short sequence, but we don't have any kind of direct reference to anything that is set on the planet. So for us, one of the interesting challenges was really diving deep in the archives and the work of the set designers and the prop makers and deconstructing all of it just really down to the techniques, the shape language, the forms, and the materials, and then thinking, okay, how would all of that apply to the set that's based on the planet? How would they approach building these spaces if they had to build not a spaceship, but a space on the planet's surface?

So there are obviously some assumptions that we are making with our creative [team] because there is no direct source material. It's different from making the first game that was a spaceship. But I think we landed in a really good spot, and it was just a fun challenge to take on.

IGN: You were talking just now about how you had ideas for Alien Isolation 2 before you had 1. Do you have an idea for Alien Isolation 3 right now?

articles.title: Former Xbox COO Helen Chiang Speaks Out Following Shock Exit From Microsoft
articles.summary: On November 2, former Xbox COO Helen Chiang took to LinkedIn to “set the record straight” about rumors over her exit from Microsoft.
articles.body:
On November 2, former Xbox COO Helen Chiang took to LinkedIn to “set the record straight” about rumors over her exit from Microsoft.

Chiang, who was promoted as Xbox’s first-ever chief operating officer in July, had been with the company for 21 years, previously serving as the head of Minecraft. Her exit from the role in late October — just three months after the position was created — came as a shock to both industry veterans and fans alike.

Eurogamer reported that Chiang had allegedly been "terminated for policy violations." A week later, Chiang spoke out to share her side of the story in a lengthy post on LinkedIn titled "Clarity is Kindness."

In her post, Chiang said rumors of this supposed policy violation were “not accurate,” and claimed that the discourse surrounding her departure from Xbox has “created a picture of me that I hardly recognize.”

She strongly denied accusations of “leaking confidential company information to the press,” saying she’s never spoken to journalists outside of interviews approved by Xbox. She also denied rumors that she left the company to join a competitor, and pushed back on allegations of “engaging in discrimination, bullying, harassment, insider trading, embezzlement, or other fraudulent activity,” or leaving because she was “passed over for a bigger role.”

“I stand by my record: both the results I delivered and the way I have treated people throughout my career. I won’t let speculation define my character or erase that record,” she wrote.

“I believe in fairness, accountability, and holding ourselves to the standards we expect of others. Those standards only mean something when they’re applied consistently. I have serious concerns about how they were applied in my case, and I believe those concerns deserve to be taken seriously.

“I share this because I don’t want my departure reduced to an inaccurate story about incompetence, ambition for the next big job, or a Nelson-level scandal. My story is about staying true to your core values, especially when it is hard. That’s the legacy I hope to leave behind.”

She ended her post by saying that this was “not how I ever imagined my story here would end,” saying, “it is not the whole story.”

Chiang's exit was confirmed by an internal memo obtained by The Verge on October 23. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma mentioned the news in a brief statement within the memo, writing: “Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today. I’m grateful for her years of service and wish her well. We’ll share more on COO leadership as plans are finalized.”

Chiang's promotion was announced amid the news of Xbox's massive restructuring in the summer. In a statement, Sharma praised Chiang for her tenure at the company, saying, “Over nearly two decades at Xbox, Helen has helped build some of our most important businesses, from Xbox Live to leading Mojang and the Minecraft franchise. She will bring our businesses together under one operating model, making sure we make clear investment decisions, learn from our successes and failures, and hold ourselves accountable for results.”

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: 'No Amount of Competition Will Ever Unseat Steam' – Former Epic Games Engineer Rails Against Valve
articles.summary: Epic's rivalry with Valve isn't anything new, but while it's usually CEO Tim Sweeney taking shots at Valve, an ex-engineer posted a long list of problems Steam has caused in the industry.
articles.body:
Epic's rivalry with Valve isn't anything new, but while it's usually CEO Tim Sweeney taking shots at Valve, an ex-engineer posted a long list of problems Steam has caused in the industry.

Just last week, after posting about Valve's 30% cut that it takes off the top of game sales, ex-Epic Engineer Kiaran Ritchie wrote a long Twitter post detailing his critiques of the biggest PC games marketplace. And, really, it seems like he's throwing up his hands and accepting Valve's dominion over the ecosystem while blaming Steam users.

Ritchie says that, "even if an alternative were objectively better, by whatever metric you care about, it would still be of no interest to Steam users. They would in fact find it to be a problem and a threat to their investment." Specifically, he claims Steam users are hostile to other stores even existing, by saying, "Competition in this space is not only uninteresting to most Steam users, it's actively denigrated! The CONSEQUENCE of this situation, is that 30% of all gross revenue is siphoned out of the PC games industry into a black hole."

Epic Games has tried its hands at unseating Steam again recently, after Tim Sweeney bragged on Twitter about vibe coding a new version of the Epic Games Store that launches faster than Steam. But, while launching quickly and letting people access their library without waiting minutes is an improvement, even Ritchie doesn't feel like it'll make much of a difference.

Elsewhere in the post, Ritchie says, "The Steam client and infrastructure is somewhere between 'not that hard' and 'trivial.' It's a download service attached to a payment processor with a smattering of services on the side. Cloud providers handle all the infrastructure these days." But even if someone makes a 'better' client, he says, "Steam users love Steam and having their whole library in one place. It works. It's dependable. It has sales, and cards, and achievements, oh my!"

This all comes on top of Epic's years-long battle to lower the amount of cash marketplaces take from digital sales. Epic hasn't only fought Valve on this; the company has also taken on Apple and Google in its quest to get Fortnite on mobile devices – and then had to pay Apple $6 million , but won against Google .

But with Valve, Epic's problem seems to be that most gamers prefer Steam outright. After all, there are dozens of game stores on PC where people can buy games, but as Ritchie points out, Steam users are happy just sticking with Valve's store. And no matter what Epic does, that probably isn't going to change .

articles.title: Call of Duty: Warzone Is Adding a Weather System This Week
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Warzone is adding a weather system that will make every match feel a bit different.
articles.body:
Call of Duty: Warzone is adding a weather system that will make every match feel a bit different.

Later this week, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's Season 1 update will be released, and with it will come big changes to Warzone. Developer Raven Software is adding a bunch of content that matches the mechanics and tone Modern Warfare 4 brought to the franchise last month. One of the biggest things that's coming to Warzone is a new weather system, which means the map might have rain, wind, or other effects when you drop in.

It sounds like the weather will be determined before you ever load into the match, so don't expect weather cycles as you'd see in a game like Grand Theft Auto. The goal is to make it so Warzone matches feel different every time you play, as the battle royale's maps have been pretty stagnant for the last six years. The weather never changes, which can eventually make the maps feel a bit boring. However, this may make the game feel consistently interesting, and something like rain may have slight changes to gameplay. It could impact visibility, make your footsteps louder as they splash in puddles, and more.

Earlier this fall, Wardogs also added weather to multiplayer matches , which had some big changes for the gameplay. It's a worthy change to Call of Duty's battle royale and one that fans have wanted to see for some time. Fans have also wanted to see a day/night cycle as well, which could make something like night-vision goggles a meaningful piece of gear. NVGs are part of the game's DMZ extraction mode, though they're primarily used for enclosed facilities that have no power.

The new Call of Duty: Warzone update will launch with two new maps on November 6 as part of Modern Warfare 4 Season 1.

articles.title: Ben Wang Reportedly in Talks to Play Iceman in MCU X-Men Reboot
articles.summary: The Long Walk actor Ben Wang is reportedly in talks to play Iceman in the MCU's upcoming X-Men reboot.
articles.body:
The Long Walk actor Ben Wang is reportedly in talks to play Iceman in the MCU's upcoming X-Men reboot.

Deadline reported that Wang, who will soon appear as Wyatt Callow in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping , is circling the role of Marvel's icy mutant hero, Bobby Drake. He's said to be one of a few other names who have tested for the part, with other allegedly interested names including Gabriel LaBelle (The Fabelmans), Jackson Kelly (The Pitt), and Rhenzy Feliz (The Penguin).

More than anything, news of Wang's potential involvement suggests Marvel at least has plans for Iceman to play a role in the 2028 X-Men film. The character may not have the star power of a Wolverine or Cyclops, but he's remained an important figure in the comic book history for decades. In addition to a variety of appearances throughout animated projects and video games, he was famously played by Shawn Ashmore in live-action movies like the original 2000 X-Men, its two sequels, and X-Men: Days of Future Past.

Wang has found his way to more than a few notable roles in his relatively short amount of time in Hollywood. After playing smaller parts in projects like the MacGyver reboot series, The Last O.G., and 2023's Sight, the actor went on to show up in 2024's Mean Girls and Karate Kid: Legends.

Audiences really started to catch on when he played Hank Olson in the gruesome 2025 adaptation of Stephen King's The Long Walk, with even more set to see what he can do in The Hunger Games prequel later this month. X-Men will surely only open that door further should talks proceed accordingly.

Marvel has already confirmed a small collection of heavy hitters for its upcoming take on classic superhero characters. The list so far includes Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Sadie Sink as Jean Grey , Adam Driver as Mister Sinister, Christopher Abbott as Professor X, Kit Connor as Cyclops , Maya Boyd as Storm, and Samara Weaving as Emma Frost . Gen V actor Asa Germann was reported to have joined as Angel in September.

X-Men is being directed by Thunderbolts* director Jake Schreier and is scheduled to come to theaters May 5, 2028. For now, we'll have to wait to see if Wang lands the part. In the meantime, the old-school X-Men are set to kick off one last hurrah with the release of next month's Avengers: Doomsday . Whether or not Ashmore's Iceman will return for that team-up film remains to be seen.

articles.summary: There are numerous factions and NPCs you'll encounter while playing Probably Stolen. If you play your cards right, many of these factions can be on your
articles.body:
There are numerous factions and NPCs you'll encounter while playing Probably Stolen . If you play your cards right, many of these factions can be on your side and provide you with benefits. However, there's also the chance you could cross them, and then they become more trouble than you know what to do with in the future. The same goes for certain characters you might. Here's what you need to know about all factions and NPCs you can encounter while playing Probably Stolen.

These are the larger known factions you can find in Probably Stolen.

The Black Market has to do with the various thieves and criminals who approach your vendor. You might not notice them too often if you're not selling contraband or illegal items, but once you do, they start to show up more often. They'll try selling to you and buying any items that you have available. You'll want to have a Smuggler's Hold when dealing with this faction because many of the items are hot and will be seized if Security does an inspection.

You can lower your standing with this group if you attempt to sell a falsely labeled item, or you try to barter too much. Alternatively, buying low from them and offering them deals is a good way to increase your standing. As this goes up, the Black Market group will send more thieves to do deals with you, and provide notice of upcoming Black Market events.

The Lower Level factions are the most notable and frequent customers you're going to get in Probably Stolen. These characters range from addicts to scavengers, traders, or people trying to live their lives, making what they can. Because you'll be frequently dealing with them, expect your reputation with them to go up and down frequently.

You can increase your relationship with this faction by offering them deals, or buying their items and paying more. However, you can lose faction with them if you call out items they're selling as fake when they're real, or they find out you're selling them fake or mislabeled products. It is possible for your faction to go too low with this group, and if it does, they kill you, forcing you to start over.

The Revolution is starkly against the Security faction. The Revolution is trying to lay low, with many of their notable members on the Wanted list, such as Odin Haraldsson, Leroy, and Arthur Lafleur. They'll regularly appear in front of you looking for supplies to buy or trade. Although they are harmless to you (if you don't antagonize them), the Security is looking for these members and offers rewards for their capture.

Helping the Revolution can provide a negative relationship with Security, but it's not 1:1. You can work alongside these members if you're careful, and provide them aid. Alternatively, you can go against them, getting these high-level members caught by the Security. However, similar to Security, if you go too low with this faction, they do kill you and end the run.

The Security faction can be the tougher people to work alongside while playing Probably Stolen. This faction enforces the law, and if you're caught with contraband or found guilty of crimes on the Lower Levels, this lowers the faction's standing with Security. However, defeating Augs, trading and selling with the Security, or turning in any of the criminals on the Wanted list can increase your relationship with them.

By increasing your relationship with the Security officers, thieves are less likely to visit your store, the Merchant officers visit more often, and they'll perform inspections less frequently with more advanced notice about their arrival. However, if it becomes negative enough, the inspections increase, they don't respond to your alarms, and they'll eventually arrest you, ending your run.

The Upper Levels faction has to do with the richer people who live in a different part of the station. They've arrived at your store because they're stuck down in this part, or they wanted to visit it. It's easy to get by tricking these characters into buying certain items of lesser quality, as they might not be able to tell the difference.

Gaining reputation with the Upper Level characters means they have a higher chance of visiting your store, a representative can appear there every so often, or at least one customer a day will be someone from the Upper Level. However, if you cross them, they'll report your store to Security, meaning you lose reputation faster with them, and inspections take longer.

There are a handful of notable NPCs that you can encounter while playing. A handful of them are from the most Wanted list, and some are regular customers trying to make a living.

Georgio is a recurring character who you'll see regardless of what run you do. He's a quirky individual who offers to sell you odds and ends, along with the occasional piece of gold in his pile of junk. He's not a character who's out to get you, and is more there to provide support if you buy into his unique perspective on the ward.

He can be a little frustrating and a little too helpful. For example, he'll bring back the Radioactive Waste that you dispose of in the Dumping Grounds, but he's also willing to provide help for you there if you buy him, protecting you from harm for a few days. Overall, Georgio is a good character to work with and buy from if he has something worthwhile for sale.

Joe Wild is the NPC who is going to sell you passive upgrades and provide you connections throughout the Lower Levels. You can talk to him or give him a call whenever you want to buy a passive upgrade to help boost your sales, or get a new way to make money through a startup venture. Make sure to check in with Joe every few days to see what he has for sale, or he'll stop by and check in on you.

Eleanor is a stranded Upper Levels woman whose mom has been framed and is in jail. Rather than share her fate, she's found herself in the Lower Levels and is trying to survive. She seeks out your shop in hopes of one day hiring a Private Detective to help her clear her mom's name and figure out what happened. How you choose to help her is up to you, and there are several different ways her life can go based on what you do.

You'll receive a list of nine different NPCs who you want to look out for while you're working in the Lower Levels. These characters will appear in front of your vendor looking to buy or sell certain items. When they come across you, you'll have an option to turn them in to Security, or let them go and continue working with them. Having them arrested can put you at odds with certain factions, but it could be a better choice than being under scrutiny from Security.

articles.title: Here's Every New LEGO Set Releasing in November
articles.summary: Only four new LEGO sets are releasing in early November, but a mystery set will be released on Black Friday.
articles.body:
November has arrived, bringing with it – well, a few new LEGO sets. Four are out now. A mystery set releasing on Black Friday will be announced soon. But even if LEGO releases have slowed to a trickle as the end of the year draws near, the sets coming out this month are all excellent in their own right. From Dragon Ball to Barcelona, here’s every new LEGO set releasing in November 2026.

If you don't want the blurbs, you can jump right to the official listings at the LEGO Store above.

Available now for LEGO Insiders ( sign up here for free ) and November 4 for everyone else is LEGO Dragon Ball: Shenron & Goku. This set depicts the moment when all seven Dragon Balls are gathered together and the dragon Shenron bursts forth. Shenron is posed in a dynamic coil position, and the Kid Goku minifigure can fly around on the Kintoun. This set looks awesome for Dragon Ball fans.

The Sagrada Família in Barcelona is one of the most distinctive buildings in the entire world – so of course it deserves a LEGO Architecture set of its own. Earlier this year, after 144 years of being under construction, the Antoni Gaudí-designed cathedral finally reached its full structural height , making now a perfect time to celebrate by putting together a miniature version of the iconic Catholic Basilica. Just know that, at 12,060 pieces, this is biggest set by piece count LEGO has ever released. So prepare to spend many hours putting it together.

Wouldn’t it be nice to take a vacation to Italy right about now? If you build this sizable recreation of a Vatican neighborhood, you can sort of feel like you’re there. From the architecture to the canals, this LEGO Icons set oozes Venetian relaxation. It’s pricy, but it has a high piece count to match.

Finally, LEGO has released a silly and adorable new Botanicals set called Cozy Plants. It looks how it sounds, with cute little anthropomorphic pots smiling as they hold their flowers. At $22.99, this is by far the most affordable new set released this month.

Between now and November 8, three “Gift Witch Purchase” sets are available for free if you buy select sets from the LEGO Store. The first is LEGO Build, Paint and Play , which is free with any purchase of $130 or more. Next, if you buy the Venetian Neighborhood set, you’ll get LEGO Venetian Water Taxi for free. Finally, buying select Harry Potter LEGO sets ( see all qualifying sets here ) gets you a free LEGO Harry Potter Dumbledore’s Office with Harry Potter set.

All Gift With Purchase sets are available while supplies last, and they often sell out before their end dates. So grab what you want sooner than later if it qualifies you for a GWP.

The Black Friday LEGO Set Will Probably Be Announced Soon

Each year, LEGO releases a big new set on Black Friday . This year, that falls on November 27. There have been plenty of rumors and speculation surrounding this year’s Black Friday set, but LEGO hasn’t officially announced it yet. According to my research (i.e. a little light Googling), last year’s Black Friday set, LEGO Star Trek U.S.S. Enterprise was announced on November 6, 2025. If that pattern holds, the announcement should be coming up soon. Stay tuned.

For a full rundown of all upcoming sets announced so far, check out our list of upcoming LEGO release dates .

articles.title: Alien: Isolation 2 Sticking With Pure Survival Horror Roots, Says Creative Director
articles.summary: Alien Isolation 2 will be released in 2027, ready to remind you why xenomorphs are pure nightmare fuel. At the Lucca Comics and Games Festival IGN sat down with the game's creative director, Al Hope, who explained the core vision behind the science fiction sequel and why the team was sticking with the survival horror genre.
articles.body:
Alien: Isolation 2 will be released in 2027, ready to remind you why xenomorphs are pure nightmare fuel. At the Lucca Comics and Games Festival IGN sat down with the game's creative director, Al Hope, who explained the core vision behind the science fiction sequel and why the team was sticking with the survival horror genre.

"We feel like there's still so much to mine or tap into in the universe of that first movie," he said. "We feel like in Alien: Isolation 2, I think the promise is about transporting you back to that time and place, that window of the timeline where just one alien can be absolutely terrifying and an incredible challenge, an incredible experience."

The original Alien: Isolation , released in 2014, had engineer Amanda (daughter of Ellen) Ripley as its star, as she searched for clues relating to her mother's disappearance on the space station Sevastopol. We've already heard Andrea Deck, Ripley’s voice actor, during a press demo for the sequel, but Hope was keen to underline the fact that Alien Isolation 2 is very focused on its new protagonist.

"We're really proud of Amanda, but to be clear, you're playing as a new character in Isolation 2... She works for the company; she hasn't encountered the creature before. And so yeah, I guess we're super excited about Blake."

We know a little about Blake already. She's a manager at Weyland-Yutani and has just arrived on planet LV-921 in search of the lab that was jettisoned from Sevastopol Station by Amanda Ripley, complete with a xenomorph hanging around inside.

You can read the full interview with Creative Director Al Hope and Project Art Director Ana Sopikova here , where we also talk xenomorph design, seeing the first game's save stations appear in Alien: Romulus , and whether or not the games are now part of the official Alien canon.
